meta.question: 大学学术写作课是否应该允许学生使用 AI 写作助手（如 ChatGPT）辅助写作并提供形成性反馈？应当如何引入？

research_frame.question: 大学学术写作课是否应该允许学生使用 AI 写作助手（如 ChatGPT）辅助写作并提供形成性反馈？应当如何引入？
research_frame.success_condition: independent writing ability improves or does not decline on no-AI assessments while AI dependency, academic integrity risk and false confidence stay controlled; evidence base supports a bounded pilot.

decision.decision_question: 大学学术写作课是否应该允许学生使用 AI 写作助手（如 ChatGPT）辅助写作并提供形成性反馈？
decision.target_population: university undergraduate students enrolled in academic writing courses
decision.target_context: university academic writing course (16-week semester), scaffolded formative-feedback instruction, instructor feedback available, offline
supported_claims: Using ChatGPT as a formative feedback tool can significantly improve short-term academic writing scores and is positively perceived by students (E-001, E-002).
Guardrail design (hints and feedback instead of answers) eliminates the negative learning effect of unguarded AI access (E-004).
Interactive AI homework can raise engagement and satisfaction without harming learning outcomes (E-007, E-008).
Task/assignment scores must not be equated with independent writing ability (E-003, E-005).
uncertain_claims: Whether AI-assisted writing instruction improves or preserves long-term independent writing ability in university students — no direct evidence; E-003 (subject-mismatched) is the only independent-performance signal.
Whether the 6-hour Marzuki effect extends to a full semester (E-001).
Whether engagement gains from high school ESL homework (Lee) generalize to university academic writing courses (E-007, E-008).
contradicted_claims: The claim that 'AI writing assistants always improve independent writing performance' is contradicted by E-003 (unguarded access → 17% worse independent exam performance).
decision.reason_for_disagreement: Disagreement comes from outcome separation (task/assignment scores vs independent ability), tool design (guarded feedback vs unguarded generation), and population (high school vs university). Writing-context evidence (Marzuki) is positive but short and uncontrolled; the strongest evidence (Bastani) shows unguarded AI harms independent performance but in a different subject and level.
decision.methodology_summary: One mixed-methods university writing study (Marzuki 2024: no randomization, 6-hour intervention, delayed test), one large high-school mathematics RCT (Bastani 2025: task-vs-learning separation, guardrail comparison), and one high-school ESL RCT (Lee 2025: engagement plus non-inferior learning). No randomized university-level academic writing study with a no-AI independent writing transfer test exists in the reviewed set.

outcome_specific_findings.knowledge_gain: positive short-term writing-skill gain with AI feedback (E-001); non-inferior with a significant gain in one group for ESL homework (E-008)
outcome_specific_findings.independent_problem_solving: negative for unguarded access, neutralized by guardrails (E-003, E-004); never measured in a university writing context
outcome_specific_findings.assignment_score: improves during practice but does not transfer to independent performance (E-005)
outcome_specific_findings.engagement: positive for AI interactive homework (E-007) and positive student perceptions of AI feedback (E-002)
outcome_specific_findings.ai_dependency: documented crutch behavior with unguarded access (E-006)

decision.short_term_effect: Positive: AI-assisted formative feedback improves short-term writing scores (E-001) and engagement (E-002, E-007).
decision.long_term_effect: Unknown: no university writing study measures independent writing ability beyond the intervention; Marzuki's delayed test follows only a 6-hour intervention (E-001).
decision.transfer_effect: Negative evidence from mathematics warns that task gains do not transfer to independent performance (E-003, E-005); no university writing transfer test exists.
decision.risk_effect: AI dependency, academic-integrity violations and false confidence are real risks for unguarded usage (E-006); guardrail design mitigates the negative learning effect (E-004).

applicability.suitable_for: bounded pilot in a university academic writing course with a guardrailed AI usage policy and independent no-AI writing assessment
applicability.not_suitable_for: unrestricted student AI use without a usage policy or integrity safeguards
required_conditions: academic integrity policy covering AI-assisted writing

what_can_be_claimed: AI writing assistants used as formative feedback tools can improve short-term academic writing scores and are positively perceived by students.
Unguarded generative AI access carries a real risk of harming independent performance when the AI is removed.
Guardrail design (feedback/hints instead of answers) substantially mitigates that risk.
AI interactive homework can improve engagement without harming learning outcomes.
Direct evidence about university academic writing independent ability is missing.
what_cannot_be_claimed: AI writing assistants improve (or even preserve) university students' long-term independent writing ability.
Any semester-long academic writing outcome based on a 6-hour intervention.
That writing/assignment score gains reflect genuine independent writing skill rather than AI-supported task performance.
Any claim about academic-integrity outcomes, which none of the three studies directly measured.
missing_evidence: Randomized or matched-section study of AI writing assistants in university academic writing courses with a no-AI independent writing transfer test.
Studies varying AI usage policy (guardrailed feedback vs open generation) within a writing course.
Longitudinal data on AI dependency and academic integrity in university writing beyond one course.
Retention evidence for writing outcomes beyond a few weeks.
decision.decision_rationale: Writing-context evidence is positive but short and uncontrolled; strong general evidence warns that unguarded AI harms independent performance; and no university writing study measures independent ability. A bounded, guardrailed, 4-phase pilot with an independent no-AI writing transfer test is the evidence-consistent action.
exceeds_evidence_boundary: 'AI 写作助手能提高大学生的独立写作能力' — exceeds: no university writing study measures independent no-AI writing ability.
'AI 写作助手对学术诚信无风险' — exceeds: no reviewed study measured academic-integrity outcomes.
'AI 辅助写作的分数提升等于写作能力提升' — exceeds: task performance and independent ability are demonstrably distinct (E-003, E-005).

claims.claim: Using ChatGPT as a formative feedback tool significantly improved university ESL students' academic writing skills across pre/post/delayed tests.
Students reported positive perceptions of ChatGPT as a feedback tool, using it to improve assignment quality and writing efficiency.

Unguarded generative AI access (GPT Base) improved practice performance (+48%) but lowered independent exam performance by 17% relative to control — contradicting the claim that AI access reliably improves independent performance.
Teacher-designed guardrails (GPT Tutor: hints instead of answers) largely eliminated the negative effect of AI on independent exam performance.

Task performance during practice improves sharply with AI access (+48% GPT Base, +127% GPT Tutor), yet these gains do not transfer to independent exam performance — assignment/writing scores must not be equated with independent ability.
Students treated unguarded GPT Base as a crutch during practice, and this reliance was associated with worse independent performance — a documented AI dependency mechanism.
GPT-4 interactive homework produced higher student satisfaction and stronger intention to continue using it than traditional homework.
Replacing traditional homework with GPT-4 interactive homework did not harm learning outcomes, and one group achieved significantly better learning gains.

study_audits.study_design: mixed methods intervention study: pre/post/delayed writing tests plus questionnaires and focus groups

control_group.note: Comparison group of 56 students received traditional writing instruction without ChatGPT.

randomization.note: No random assignment; group allocation raises self-selection risk.

transfer_test.note: No independent no-AI writing transfer test; all outcomes measured while ChatGPT usage was part of the condition.

sample_bias.note: Final analysis 35 EG + 37 CG (72) from 78 + 56 initial enrolments.

self_selection.note: Consent-based participation; students may self-select into the experimental group.

measurement_validity.note: Rubric-scored writing tests with pre/post/delayed structure, triangulated by questionnaires and focus groups.

confounders.note: Novelty effect and single-institution context not controlled.

instructor_effect.note: Single institution; instructor assignment across groups not detailed.

novelty_effect.note: 6-hour intervention is very short; novelty likely inflates perceived benefit.

ai_usage_policy.note: ChatGPT deployed as a formative feedback tool, but precise usage boundaries are not fully specified.

dropout.note: Attrition from 78/56 to 35/37 final analysed; reasons not detailed.

task_vs_learning_guard.measured_construct: rubric-scored writing test performance in a formative-feedback condition
task_vs_learning_guard.note: Improved writing scores may partly reflect AI-supported task performance rather than independent writing ability; without a no-AI independent writing assessment, writing score gain cannot be equated with independent writing skill gain.

limitations: No independent no-AI writing transfer test
Attrition between initial and final samples not fully explained
suggestions: Extend intervention duration to a full term
Add an independent no-AI writing transfer assessment
Report dropout reasons and usage-fidelity data

study_audits.study_design: large-scale three-arm randomized controlled trial (no AI / GPT Base unguarded / GPT Tutor guardrailed)

post_test.note: Practice performance and independent exam measured.

transfer_test.note: Independent closed-book exam functions as a transfer check from practice, but no longer-term transfer measure.

measurement_validity.note: Independent exam without AI access cleanly separates task performance from learning.

confounders.note: Three-arm design isolates the effect of tool design.

instructor_effect.note: Standardized study sessions; instructor effects minimized.

novelty_effect.note: Short in-class sessions; novelty not explicitly controlled.

ai_usage_policy.note: Explicit contrast between unguarded (GPT Base) and guardrailed (GPT Tutor) usage.

dropout.note: Not reported in the reviewed summary.

task_vs_learning_guard.measured_construct: practice problem performance vs independent closed-book exam performance
task_vs_learning_guard.note: The study itself demonstrates the dissociation: +48%/+127% practice performance coexisted with -17% independent exam performance in the unguarded arm.

limitations: Subject mismatch: high school mathematics, not university academic writing
No positive learning gain even with guardrails (they eliminate harm, do not produce gain)
suggestions: Replicate the guardrail design in a writing context

randomization.note: Randomized controlled trial at class level.

pre_test.note: Baseline learning levels measured; detail limited in the reviewed summary.

post_test.note: Learning outcome assessments and engagement measures collected.

instructor_effect.note: Four classes; instructor differences across classes not fully controlled.

novelty_effect.note: Novel interactive platform may inflate engagement.

ai_usage_policy.note: Interactive homework tutor design defined, but guardrail details limited in the reviewed summary.

dropout.note: Not reported in the reviewed summary.

task_vs_learning_guard.note: Learning outcomes are measured separately from engagement, which is a strength; but no independent no-AI writing transfer test exists.

limitations: High school ESL context, not university academic writing
Homework-only setting does not cover the classroom writing process
suggestions: Extend to university academic writing with classroom writing tasks
Add retention and no-AI transfer assessments

control_group.note: All three studies include a no-AI or traditional-instruction comparison.

randomization.note: Bastani 2025 and Lee 2025 randomized; Marzuki 2024 did not.

pre_test.note: Marzuki has pre/post/delayed tests; Bastani and Lee measure baselines.

post_test.note: Immediate outcome measures present in all studies.

retention_test.note: Only Marzuki 2024 includes a delayed test; Bastani and Lee have none.

transfer_test.note: No study tests independent no-AI writing in a university context; Bastani's independent exam is the closest analogue but in mathematics.

sample_bias.note: Bastani is large; Lee is four classes; Marzuki is a single elite private university.

self_selection.note: Marzuki consent-based; Bastani and Lee randomized.

measurement_validity.note: Task performance is separated from independent performance only in Bastani 2025.

confounders.note: Novelty effects, tool versions and instructor effects not fully controlled across the set.

instructor_effect.note: Marzuki single institution; Lee across four classes; Bastani standardized sessions.

novelty_effect.note: Short interventions in all three studies likely inflate engagement.

tool_version_effect.note: ChatGPT/GPT-4 versions differ across studies and continue to evolve.

ai_usage_policy.note: Only Bastani explicitly contrasts unguarded vs guardrailed usage policies.

task_vs_learning_guard.measured_construct: writing/assignment scores vs independent writing ability
task_vs_learning_guard.note: Writing scores or assignment scores must NOT be equated with independent writing ability. Bastani 2025 shows +48-127% task performance coexisting with -17% independent exam performance; Marzuki's improved writing scores under a ChatGPT-feedback condition carry the same risk of reflecting AI-supported task performance rather than independent writing skill.

limitations: No university-level academic writing RCT measuring independent no-AI writing ability.
Bastani 2025 is methodologically strong but in high school mathematics; subject directness to university academic writing is low.
Lee 2025 is a high school ESL RCT with no retention or transfer test.
Marzuki 2024 is the only writing-context study but lacks randomization, is single-institution, and has no transfer assessment.
suggestions: Design a randomized or matched-section pilot in university academic writing with an independent no-AI writing transfer test.
Adopt guardrail principles from Bastani's GPT Tutor (feedback/hints instead of answers) for the writing context.
Measure process (AI usage logs, reflections) alongside learning and risk outcomes.
Separate task/assignment performance metrics from independent learning metrics in all analyses.

conflicts.reason_for_disagreement: Disagreement comes from outcome separation (task/assignment scores vs independent ability), tool design (guarded feedback vs unguarded generation), and population (high school vs university). Writing-context evidence (Marzuki) is positive but short and uncontrolled; the strongest evidence (Bastani) shows unguarded AI harms independent performance but in a different subject and level.

applicability.suitable_for: bounded pilot in a university academic writing course with a guardrailed AI usage policy and independent no-AI writing assessment
applicability.not_suitable_for: unrestricted student AI use without a usage policy or integrity safeguards
required_conditions: academic integrity policy covering AI-assisted writing

intervention.target_learners: university undergraduate students in an academic writing course (1-2 sections, ~30-60 students, including ESL learners)
learning_goals: independently plan, draft and revise academic writing without AI
use AI writing assistants critically as formative feedback and error-explanation tools, not as text generators
develop reflection skills: explain every AI-assisted change in their own words

phase_1.name: Phase 1 — Independent Drafting (No AI)
activities: weeks 1-2: students draft essays with no AI access whatsoever
phase_1.ai_usage_rule: all AI usage forbidden; drafts must be entirely student-written
phase_1.outcome_check: baseline independent writing quality and no-AI baseline score

phase_2.name: Phase 2 — AI Feedback and Error Explanation Only
activities: weeks 3-4: AI allowed to give feedback on student drafts and explain grammar/style errors; it must not generate new text
phase_2.ai_usage_rule: AI may give formative feedback and explain errors only; no generation or rewriting of passages
phase_2.outcome_check: mid-pilot in-class writing sample without AI; student reflection on which feedback was applied

phase_3.name: Phase 3 — AI-Assisted Revision with Explanation
activities: weeks 5-7: AI may suggest revisions; students must accept/reject each suggestion and justify their choices in a revision memo
phase_3.ai_usage_rule: AI-assisted revision allowed only with a mandatory revision memo explaining every AI-suggested change that was kept
phase_3.outcome_check: weekly draft quality rubric plus revision-memo completeness

phase_4.name: Phase 4 — Independent Writing Transfer Test (No AI)
activities: week 8: a new academic writing task on an unseen topic completed in a strictly no-AI environment
phase_4.ai_usage_rule: no AI access during the transfer assessment
phase_4.outcome_check: independent writing score and transfer-task rubric

intervention.ai_usage_policy: AI usage is restricted to three explicitly graded modes: no-AI drafting (phase 1), feedback/error-explanation only (phase 2), AI-assisted revision with mandatory explanation (phase 3). Copying AI-generated text into a submission without explanation is an academic integrity violation. A no-AI transfer assessment closes the pilot (phase 4).
intervention.teacher_role: design guardrailed feedback prompts and rubrics; review AI usage logs and revision memos weekly; hold short reflection debriefs
intervention.student_role: draft independently in phase 1; use AI only for feedback in phase 2; revise with AI while documenting every change in phase 3; complete the independent no-AI transfer task in phase 4
intervention.reflection_requirement: students must explain every AI-assisted change in their own words (revision memo); one written reflection per phase on when AI helped versus when it masked understanding
intervention.assessment: no-AI baseline writing assessment, mid-pilot in-class writing sample, draft quality rubric, independent no-AI writing transfer task, revision memos, AI usage self-report
risk_control: guardrailed usage policy modeled on Bastani 2025 GPT Tutor (feedback/hints instead of answers)
independent no-AI writing transfer test prevents score inflation from AI-supported task performance
revision memos and usage logs reviewed weekly to detect AI dependency
academic integrity policy explicitly covers AI-generated text and unexamined copying
false-confidence check: predicted grade vs actual grade on no-AI assessments
stop_conditions: independent writing transfer-test scores drop significantly below baseline/cohort expectations
revision memos show widespread unexamined AI copying (integrity violations in >20% of submissions)
AI dependency signals (usage without understanding, explanation quality) exceed threshold for two consecutive weeks
teacher workload for reviewing memos/logs becomes unsustainable

evaluation.research_question: In a university academic writing course, does a guardrailed AI writing assistant (feedback-only → AI-assisted revision with explanation) improve independent writing ability without increasing AI dependency, academic-integrity risk, or false confidence, compared to traditional no-AI writing instruction?

groups.treatment: one section using the 4-phase guardrailed AI writing-assistant policy
groups.comparison: one matched section without AI access (same instructor, materials and rubrics)

evaluation.baseline: week-1 independent writing assessment in a strictly no-AI environment (writing quality rubric, fluency, grammar/accuracy)
evaluation.post_test: week-8 independent writing assessment in a no-AI environment (same rubric as baseline)
evaluation.retention_test: delayed writing task 4-6 weeks after the pilot ends, in a no-AI environment
evaluation.transfer_test: week-8 novel academic writing task on an unseen topic in a strictly no-AI environment
process_metrics: AI usage logs: prompts submitted, feedback requested, accepted vs rejected suggestions
revision memo completeness and explanation quality
help-seeking behaviour: self-generated revision vs AI-suggested revision ratio
draft revision counts and writing fluency measures
learning_metrics: independent writing score on no-AI assessments (baseline / post / retention / transfer)
writing quality rubric (structure, argument, grammar, vocabulary)
retention on the delayed no-AI writing task
risk_metrics: ai_dependency: usage-without-understanding index from revision-memo quality and ratio of unexplained AI edits
academic_integrity_risk: detected copying of AI-generated text without attribution/explanation; integrity violations per submission
false_confidence: predicted grade vs actual grade gap on no-AI assessments; self-reported confidence vs independent performance
evaluation.analysis_plan: Pre-registered comparison of treatment vs comparison sections on baseline-adjusted learning metrics (ANCOVA); learning metrics (no-AI independent writing) analysed separately from process/task metrics; subgroup analysis by initial writing proficiency; risk metrics monitored weekly with stop-condition checks at weeks 3, 5, 7 and at the transfer test.
evaluation.success_threshold: treatment shows non-inferior independent writing (delta within 5%) AND equal or better retention AND AI dependency index and integrity violations below thresholds; if independent writing declines >10% on the transfer test, the pilot is judged unsuccessful regardless of in-class score gains.
stop_conditions: independent writing transfer-test decline >10% vs comparison
integrity violations (unexplained AI copying) in >20% of submissions
ai_dependency index exceeding the pre-set threshold for two consecutive weeks
false-confidence gap widening beyond the pre-set bound across two consecutive assessments
